core.title: Declare DTOs in the contracts location
core.given: A source file that the stack's role assignment assigns to a layer role (any layer, not only a feature's), and that is not in the contracts location
core.when: a type recognized as a DTO by the stack's DTO naming idiom is declared in or moved into it
core.then: Declare the DTO type in the contracts location (a module owned by neither side of the boundary), not inside a layer's internal code (e.g. a feature's internal layer).
prefer: Canonical placement: declare the DTO in the contracts location and import that shared boundary shape from both sides of the boundary.
During GREEN: reuse an existing contract type that already represents the payload.
During GREEN: add only the fields the current acceptance requires.
During GREEN: create a new DTO only for a genuinely distinct boundary shape.
avoid: Declaring the DTO inside a layer's internal code (e.g. a feature layer) as a temporary shortcut.
Moving unrelated internal types into the contracts location.
Another feature importing a DTO declared inside one feature's layer (a private type leak).
unless: Test files and trees excluded by the stack's scan classification (e.g. vendored and build-output trees) are never scanned.
A file assigned to no layer role is outside these rules, not in violation.
core.why: A DTO belongs to the contract (owned by neither side), not to either side; declared inside one feature's layer it becomes a private type that other features import anyway, so the boundary runs through somebody's internals.
evidence: Every affected DTO declaration lives in the contracts location.
The stack's placement check reports no DTO-placement finding for any affected DTO declaration.
verification: The check flags a DTO declaration (a type recognized by the stack's DTO naming idiom) in a scanned source file that is assigned to a layer role and not in the contracts location.

The check scans every DTO declaration in scanned files, pre-existing ones included; coder guidance fires on an added-or-moved declaration (change) or on a reported finding, combined with the file-kind and role facts.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

Test files are never scanned (file-kind scope, not a tree exclusion), and a tree is exempt only when the stack's checker classifies it as excluded; the excluded trees are one stack-wide list (profile roots.excluded) whose exact classification is owned by the stack's checker.
Imports of external packages resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked (import-resolution exception); this does not exempt a locally declared DTO.
A file carrying no layer role is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.

fires: A coder adds a DTO type in a source file assigned to a layer role and outside the contracts location (e.g. a feature's domain or application directory).
A coder moves an existing DTO declaration into a layer-assigned source file outside the contracts location.
The placement check reports an existing DTO declaration in a layer-assigned source file outside the contracts location (e.g. one another feature imports — a private type leak).
doesNotFire: A DTO declared in the contracts location.
A DTO declared in a test file (never scanned by file-kind scope) or in a tree the stack's checker excludes from scanning (e.g. a vendored or build-output tree).
A DTO in a file assigned to no layer role (outside the rules, not in violation).
A type not recognized as a DTO by the stack's DTO naming idiom.
An import of an external package (not layer-checked); this does not suppress a finding for a locally declared DTO.

profileRequirements.meaning: The location where boundary-contract shapes (DTOs) are declared: owned by neither side of the boundary, identified by a path segment or glob relative to the source root.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a path segment `contracts` (declare the DTO in `contracts/`)

profileRequirements.meaning: Name patterns by which a type is recognized as a DTO (a boundary shape).
How an import of an external package (outside the project graph) is recognised, so it can be excluded from layer checking.
Vendored and build-output trees that the check never scans; one stack-wide list whose exact classification is owned by the stack's checker. Test files are excluded by file-kind scope, not as a tree.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (DTOs are declared in a contracts location owned by neither side, never inside a layer's internal code) is fully neutral; every concrete binding comes from the profile: roles.assignment (any layer role, no feature membership required), layout.contract_paths#contracts_dir (the contracts location), idiom.dto_shape#dto_naming (what counts as a DTO), idiom.external_import (external-package imports) and roots.excluded (excluded trees). Scope edges stay checker-scoped: test files are excluded by file-kind scope, and a tree is exempt only when the stack's checker classifies it as excluded (one stack-wide list), so the core grants no broader generated-tree exemption than Bun's vendored/build scope. Per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys, the rule's own severity (3) and strict disposition (fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline) are carried in core verification. What could not be made neutral stays bunOnly: realization identifiers (detector bun_clean_architecture_detector, finding id dto-placement, term ids contracts_module/private_type_leak), the language facts (typescript/bun) and the bare npm specifier wording. 'Import' is used in the generic sense of one module depending on another; each realization binds it to its own module syntax. The during-GREEN phase guidance and the behavioral-acceptance proof were already neutral.
